item.title: Three arrested after Jones County drug investigation on Trace Road - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JONES COUNTY – Three people were arrested following a narcotics investigation at a residence on Trace Road, according to the Jones County Sheriff’s Department.

Sheriff’s narcotics agents and investigators with the department’s Criminal Investigations Division went to a home in the 300 block of Trace Road on March 23 to serve a Jones County Circuit Court bench warrant on Stephanie Williams, 51.

As officers arrived, a man identified as John Smith, 37, also known as “Smitty,” ran from the scene on foot, authorities said.

Investigators said Smith fled into a field in front of the house and threw suspected fentanyl from his pocket while running. Officers caught up with him, but said he resisted arrest and broke free before running again. He was later taken into custody after a second foot chase.

Authorities said agents found a bag of suspected methamphetamine in Smith’s pocket.

Investigators later executed a search warrant at the Trace Road residence and recovered additional narcotics, according to the sheriff’s department. That led to a charge against homeowner Richard Cockrell, 66, for possession of a controlled substance, identified as methamphetamine.

Williams, Smith and Cockrell were each charged with possession of a controlled substance. Smith also was charged with resisting arrest and disorderly conduct.

All three were taken to the Jones County Adult Detention Facility, where they remained pending an initial appearance in Jones County Justice Court.

The sheriff’s department said its Narcotics Division worked 186 felony narcotics cases in 2025. Through March 20, 2026, agents had opened 55 cases, nearly 30% of last year’s total.

item.title: Two dead in apparent domestic shooting in Verona - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
VERONA – Two people were found dead early Wednesday after a shooting tied to a domestic disturbance on Clement Street, according to Verona police and WTVA.

Police responded around 1 a.m. Wednesday to reports of gunfire on Clement Street. When officers arrived, they found two people suffering from gunshot wounds.

WTVA reported that authorities said a 32-year-old woman had been shot twice. A 28-year-old man was found with two self-inflicted gunshot wounds. Both were pronounced dead at the scene by the Lee County coroner.

Police said the shooting appears to be an isolated incident and that there is no ongoing threat to the public. The case remains under active investigation.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Verona Police Department.

item.title: Tupelo woman charged in Boggan Drive burglary case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A Tupelo woman has been charged in connection with a residential burglary reported earlier this year on Boggan Drive, according to the Tupelo Police Department.

Officers responded Jan. 8 to Boggan Drive after receiving a report of a burglary. When they arrived, they spoke with the property owner, who said an acquaintance had forced entry into the home and stolen an item from inside.

After further investigation, police arrested Alexus I. Sykes, 31, of Tupelo, on March 19 and charged her with one count of burglary of a dwelling.

During an initial court appearance on March 20, Tupelo Municipal Court Judge Allen Weir ordered Sykes held on a $5,000 bond.

Police said the case will be presented to the Lee County grand jury.

Following an investigation, police arrested Catriama Pugh, 32, and charged her with accessory after the fact.

Quanneisheia Pugh, 34, was charged with shooting into an occupied vehicle and possession of a weapon by a convicted felon.

Omarion Nelson, 20, was charged with aggravated assault with a firearm and shooting into an occupied dwelling.

Police said the case remains under investigation.

item.title: Texas Man Sentenced to 34 Years for Cocaine Trafficking in Rankin County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY — A Texas man has been sentenced to 34 years in prison after a Rankin County jury found him guilty of aggravated trafficking of cocaine, District Attorney Bubba Bramlett announced.

Jorge Rodriguez, 36, of El Paso, Texas, was convicted following a trial in Rankin County Circuit Court. He was ordered to serve the sentence day-for-day in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections without the possibility of parole.

The conviction stems from a traffic stop on Interstate 20 conducted by the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department Criminal Interdiction Unit. During the stop, deputies, assisted by a K-9 unit, discovered approximately 12 kilograms of cocaine concealed in the trunk of the vehicle Rodriguez was occupying.

Authorities said the drugs were hidden inside a tire that did not belong to the vehicle.

Prosecutors also presented testimony from a special agent with the Texas Department of Public Safety, who said Rodriguez sold him four ounces of cocaine roughly two months before the Rankin County arrest while the agent was working undercover.

“This was not a small amount of drugs or a close call — this was large-scale trafficking,” Bramlett said in a statement. “When that kind of activity comes through Rankin County, we will find it, we will prosecute it, and we will make sure those responsible face serious time.”

The district attorney’s office credited the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department, the Texas Department of Public Safety and the Mississippi Forensics Laboratory for their roles in the investigation and prosecution.

item.title: Taste of Mississippi Returns April 13 to Benefit Stewpot Community Services - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The annual Taste of Mississippi will return April 13, bringing together dozens of local restaurants, live music and community support for a longtime Jackson nonprofit.

Now in its 37th year, the event will be held from 7 to 10 p.m. at the Mississippi Trade Mart, offering both indoor and outdoor experiences. Organizers say the event will take place rain or shine.

Guests will sample food from more than 30 participating restaurants while voting for awards including Best Appetizer, Best Entrée, Best Dessert, Best Presentation and People’s Choice. Live entertainment will be provided by Aa’Keela & The Beats and The Lonely Hearts Duo.

Proceeds from the event benefit Stewpot Community Services, which provides free food, clothing and shelter to those in need. Funds raised also support the organization’s shelters, food pantry, street outreach, after-school programs and daily noon meal service.

Organizers say the event has grown over the years with support from local businesses, sponsors and attendees, raising more than $100,000 annually.

“This event is about more than great food — it’s about giving back to our community,” organizers said in a release.

Tickets are $55 for general admission, which includes unlimited tastings, and $90 for a Tasting Plus option that includes four drink tickets. The event is open to those 21 and older.

Tickets and additional information are available at stewpot.org/tasteofms.

item.title: Pike County deputies recover drugs, guns during search; suspect wanted on felony warrants - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PIKE COUNTY – Pike County authorities are searching for a man wanted on multiple felony warrants after deputies recovered narcotics, firearms and materials used to manufacture illegal substances during a search in the White Acres community.

The Pike County Sheriff’s Office said its Special Response Team, with assistance from the Parish County Line Task Force and the McComb Police Department, executed a search warrant March 23 on Sedgewick Street in White Acres.

During the search, deputies recovered narcotics, firearms and instruments used in the manufacture of illegal substances, according to the sheriff’s office. Some of the seized items field-tested positive for fentanyl.

Authorities said Dekendrick Spurlock, 41, was charged in connection with the search and is now wanted on multiple felony warrants.

Investigators said Spurlock is believed to be armed and should not be approached.

Anyone with information about his whereabouts is asked to contact Crime Stoppers at 601-869-7141 or submit a tip online through p3tips.com.

item.title: Jackson police investigate fatal shooting at Pine Garden Apartments - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Jackson police are investigating a fatal shooting that left a 20-year-old man dead Tuesday night at an apartment complex on Rebel Woods Drive.

Officers with Precinct 1 responded around 9:23 p.m. Tuesday to a report of an aggravated assault at Pine Garden Apartments in the 200 block of Rebel Woods Drive, according to police.

When officers arrived, they found Jakori Smith, 20, lying on a sidewalk with multiple gunshot wounds. He was taken to a local hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.

Detectives with the department’s Robbery/Homicide Unit and members of the Mobile Crime Unit were called to the scene.

Police said the suspects were described as three Black males. No vehicle description was available.

Investigators recovered multiple shell casings at the scene.

The case remains under investigation. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1234 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS.

item.title: GoFundMe Launched for Natchez Man Killed in Highway 61 Crash - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
NATCHEZ — A fundraiser has been launched to help cover funeral expenses for a Natchez man who was killed Sunday night after being struck by a vehicle along U.S. Highway 61.

Devon Harper, 29, died after being hit around 11 p.m. near a Walmart, according to the Mississippi Highway Patrol. Authorities said a 2019 Dodge Charger, driven by 24-year-old Elijah Marsaw of Vidalia, Louisiana, was traveling southbound when it collided with Harper, who was also walking south. Harper was pronounced dead at the scene.

In the days following his death, Harper’s brother, Frank Harper, created a GoFundMe campaign seeking assistance with cremation and funeral costs.

“I’m raising money today to help get my brother cremated and take care of funeral services,” Frank Harper wrote. “My brother was an awesome brother, a great friend, and loved life more than anybody I know.”

He said the family is asking for help as they make arrangements after the sudden loss.

“He was unfortunately struck by a vehicle … and passed on, and I can really use the help to get him cremated,” he wrote. “I thank you for taking the time to read this.”

The crash remains under investigation by the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

item.title: Fugitive wanted in Minnesota arrested in Natchez by U.S. Marshals and Adams Co. Deputies - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ADAMS COUNTY – A fugitive wanted in Minnesota on multiple felony charges was arrested Wednesday in Natchez during a joint law enforcement operation led by the U.S. Marshals Service, according to the Adams County Sheriff’s Office.

Elijah Davion York was taken into custody without incident March 25 at a house on Seale Lane in Natchez, authorities said.

York was wanted in Dakota County, Minnesota, on extraditable felony warrants that included first-degree criminal sexual conduct involving a victim younger than 14, use of a minor in sexual performance or pornographic work, fourth-degree assault against protected classes and fifth-degree assault, according to officials.

Authorities said York had also previously failed to appear in court as required.

After confirming the active warrants with the originating agency, members of the U.S. Marshals Service, assisted by Adams County sheriff’s deputies, carried out the arrest without resistance, officials said.

York is being held pending extradition proceedings to Minnesota.

The Adams County Sheriff’s Office said the arrest reflects cooperation between federal and local law enforcement agencies in locating and apprehending fugitives across state lines.

item.title: Forrest County deputies investigate animal abuse case in Petal area - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
FORREST COUNTY – The Forrest County Sheriff’s Office is investigating a possible animal abuse case after deputies found a severely emaciated dog inside an apparently abandoned home in the Petal area.

The sheriff’s office said it was notified Tuesday, March 24, of the suspected abuse.

Following an investigation, deputies located the dog inside the residence and immediately removed the animal for emergency treatment.

The dog was taken to Advanced Pet Care Animal Hospital, where veterinary staff are working to stabilize and care for it, according to the sheriff’s office.

Authorities said the investigation remains ongoing.

Anyone who wants to help with the cost of the dog’s medical treatment can contact Advanced Pet Care Animal Hospital at 601-268-1350. Donations also can be made through The Pretty Pittie Committee, a nonprofit that helps raise money for animals suffering from abuse and neglect.

The sheriff’s office said it remains committed to pursuing cases involving animal abuse and neglect.

item.title: Former Tupelo neurologist sentenced to 15 years on child pornography charge - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A former Tupelo neurologist was sentenced Tuesday to 15 years in prison after pleading guilty to possession of child pornography, according to the district attorney’s office.

Ali Ahmad entered the guilty plea March 24 in state court. Senior Circuit Court Judge Paul S. Funderburk sentenced him to 15 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections.

Because of the nature of the offense, Ahmad is not eligible for parole and must serve the sentence day for day, officials said.

Ahmad also was sentenced earlier this year in federal court. On Feb. 11, Chief U.S. District Judge Debra M. Brown sentenced him to 144 months in prison on a charge of distribution of child pornography, along with five years of supervised release and $96,100 in restitution to the victims of the offense.

Officials said the 15-year state sentence will run concurrently with the federal sentence.

According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Mississippi, Ahmad’s work visa has been revoked and he will be deported after serving his sentence.

District Attorney Jason D. Herring said the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, Detective Rachel Clock, the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office and the Department of Homeland Security assisted in the investigation.

Assistant District Attorney Josh Wise prosecuted the case for the state.

item.title: Tupelo man charged with kidnapping after allegedly holding ex-girlfriend against her will - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A Tupelo man has been charged with kidnapping following an investigation that began with a report of a woman being held against her will, police said.

According to authorities, officers responded March 18 to the area of Ballard Park in reference to a possible kidnapping. Police said an individual reported that a friend had contacted them and said she was being held against her will by her ex-boyfriend, who was possibly armed.

Officers were given a description of the vehicle involved and located it a short time later on Mitchell Road, according to police. The suspect was initially taken into custody on misdemeanor charges.

After further investigation, William H. McCord, 32, of Tupelo, was arrested March 20 and charged with one count of kidnapping.

Tupelo Municipal Judge Weir ordered McCord to be held without bond on March 20. The case will be presented to the Lee County grand jury, according to police.

item.title: Three Arrested in Jackson Robbery Spree; Each Given $6M Bond - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Three suspects were arrested Saturday in connection with a string of armed robberies, aggravated assaults and home invasions across Jackson, police said.

The arrests came March 21 after officers with Capitol Police stopped a black Honda Accord on State Street near Beasley Road. The vehicle had been identified in a “be on the lookout” alert issued by the Jackson Police Department tied to multiple violent crimes reported over several days.

Investigators believe the suspects were responsible for at least three robberies, including two incidents involving four Hispanic male victims and another involving two Indian victims in Precincts 1 and 2. Authorities also suspect the group may be linked to additional robberies involving Hispanic victims that remain under investigation.

The occupants of the vehicle were taken into custody and later interviewed by detectives. All three appeared before a municipal court judge and were each issued a $6 million bond.

Daja Logan, 23, was charged with two counts each of armed robbery, conspiracy, home invasion, aggravated assault, accessory before the fact and accessory after the fact.

Curtavious Simpson, 34, faces four counts of armed robbery, three counts of aggravated assault and two counts of home invasion.

Graig Bradley, 27, was charged with four counts of armed robbery, three counts of aggravated assault and two counts of home invasion.

The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is urged to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1234 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS.

item.title: Register now for the 2026 PowWow women's training weekend at Boondocks Firearms Training Academy - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RAYMOND — Boondocks Firearms Training Academy is working on lining up top-notch speakers and training for the 2026 PowWow, to be held April 17-18, 2026 .

The PowWow is an annual weekend of hands-on firearm training and community-building exclusively for women. The event aims to provide participants with exposure to industry-leading instructors, product demonstrations, and a supportive environment for skill development.

item.title: National Ag Day in the Capital City celebrated with cow milking contest - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
JACKSON – Today, Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce Andy Gipson and the Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce celebrated National Ag Day with a focus on dairy including cow milking competitions and Genuine Mississippi milk and ice cream from the Beason Family Farm of Neshoba County. Governor Tate Reeves proclaimed today “Agriculture Day” in the State of Mississippi.

Commissioner Gipson was joined outside Galloway United Methodist Church, across from the Mississippi Capitol, by Mississippi farmers, legislators and local media representatives. State Representative Shanda Yates, State Representative Kent McCarty, State Senator Kamesha Mumford, State Senator Jeremy England, and various local media personalities all participated in the milking contests.

“Agriculture’s role in Mississippi has never been more important. It is the number one industry in the state, the backbone of our economy and the basis of our small towns and rural communities,” said Commissioner Gipson. “We are proud to take this time to recognize our farmers, ranchers and producers on this special day – National Agriculture Day. I encourage everyone to seek out and thank your local farmers today.”

Gipson went on to highlight the U.S. Dietary Guidelines released by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), the Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce’s (MDAC) Make Mississippi Healthy Again initiative and MDAC’s Genuine MS® Program. He thanked Mississippi legislators for passing House Bill 1153 which prohibits the sale, offer for sale and the manufacture of “cell-cultured dairy products” that are derived from animal cells cultured outside of a live animal.

“We are living in a time where it seems everything is artificial, and you wonder what is real. We’ve seen everything from fake grass, astroturf, to fake meat, and now they’ve come up with lab grown, or fake, milk,” Commissioner Gipson continued. “So today, we’re especially proud to be here to celebrate agriculture, and to promote real food for real people. Thank you to our legislators for making Mississippi the first state in America to outlaw fake milk.”

Following brief remarks from Mississippi House Agriculture Committee Chairman Bill Pigott and Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman Neil Whaley, Commissioner Gipson invited the designated contestants to face off in back-to-back milking competitions with Jersey dairy cows provided by Beason Family Farm of Philadelphia. The Commissioner awarded first place trophies and bragging rights to the winners: Senator Jeremy England and Meteorologist Austin Powell, who collected the most milk within the time of two minutes. The cow milking contestants were encouraged by young people from the Galloway Children’s Center who chanted “milk that cow; milk that cow.”

Commissioner Gipson said, “Most of those children had not seen a cow in real life. None of them had seen a cow milked. Now they know where their milk and ice cream come from and they’ll remember this experience for years to come.”

Visitors and spectators were treated to fresh bottled milk and ice cream produced by the very cows on site and provided by Genuine MS® member Beason Family Farm.

View full Ag Day festivities at https://youtu.be/QL48OL5yWjo and the Ag Day proclamation signed by Governor Tate Reeves at https://agnet.mdac.ms.gov/agManage/uploads/3351.pdf .

“You are what you eat, and we are forever grateful to our farmers who grow and raise the food we consume every day,” said Gipson. “Another exciting initiative we are proud to take part in is the USDA’s national awareness campaign to highlight the ‘Product of USA’ label. This standard ensures that when consumers see the label on meat, poultry or processed egg products, it means the animal was born, raised, harvested and processed entirely within the United States. This labeling initiative to identify fresh, locally sourced food products raised right here in the U.S. not only supports our farmers, but also allows consumers to make informed, healthier decisions.”

Agriculture is the largest industry in the state of Mississippi, producing $9.5 billion in agricultural commodities last year alone. Agriculture also employs 11.4 percent of the state’s workforce and contributes to over 14 percent of the state’s overall economic activity. Mississippi currently ranks in the Top 20 in the U.S. for production of 11 agricultural commodities, including catfish, sweet potatoes, cotton, pine lumber, broilers, rice, peanuts and more.

National Ag Day was established in 1973 by the Agriculture Council of America as an effort to encourage every American to understand how food and fiber products are produced; appreciate the role agriculture plays in providing safe, abundant and affordable products; value the essential role of agriculture in maintaining a strong economy; and acknowledge and consider career opportunities in the agriculture, food and fiber industry. To learn more about National Agriculture Day, visit www.agday.org.

item.title: Mississippi DPS transfers 1960s Klan materials to state archives - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Mississippi Department of Public Safety has transferred a collection of 1960s-era Ku Klux Klan materials to the Mississippi Department of Archives and History after the items were recently discovered during preparations for a move to the agency’s new headquarters.

According to DPS, the materials include full Klan regalia and documents that were found inside a small blue suitcase. The inventory also contains charters, a spiral notebook with meeting minutes, a ledger book, a 1964 Imperial Executive Order and numerous pamphlets.

Officials said the collection includes Klan propaganda, including a pamphlet titled “The Ugly Truth about Martin Luther King,” published by United Klans of America.

The materials also include file folders containing news clippings about the Mississippi Highway Patrol, the Mississippi Department of Public Safety, former DPS Commissioner T.B. Birdsong and materials related to the Freedom Riders.

Mississippi Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell said preserving the artifacts will help document the activities of hate groups and make sure future generations better understand that history.

The Mississippi Department of Archives and History said the transfer is significant because it gives researchers broader access to records that can deepen public understanding of Ku Klux Klan activity in Mississippi during the 1960s.

Incoming MDAH Director Barry White said the materials are especially notable because they include both administrative records and propaganda from a local chapter of a secretive national organization.

MDAH said all of the materials will be processed and eventually made digitally accessible to the public, though that work could take several months. The process will include arranging, housing and describing the collection, along with preparing a catalog overview, item-level finding aid and metadata for scanned images.

item.title: Meridian police investigate fatal shooting on 36th Avenue - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Greer Vari
item.description:
MERIDIAN – An adult male was found dead late Monday night following a reported shooting in Meridian.

Officers with the Meridian Police Department responded just after 10 p.m. on March 23 to reports of shots fired in the 1300 block of 36th Avenue. Upon arrival, officers located a man in a yard suffering from an apparent gunshot wound. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

The department’s Violent Crime Unit responded and is actively investigating the incident. The victim’s body will be transported to the Mississippi Crime Laboratory for an autopsy.

“This remains an active and ongoing investigation. We are asking anyone with information to come forward and assist us as we work to determine exactly what happened,” Assistant Chief Darrell Thompson said.

Authorities are asking anyone with information to contact the Meridian Police Department or Crime Stoppers as the investigation continues.

item.title: Journalist Therese Apel to Speak on Brig. Gen. Paul Rowlett at Arkansas event - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
TRUMANN, Ark. — Mississippi crime journalist and media personality Therese Apel will deliver the keynote address Monday at the Trumann Area Chamber of Commerce Annual Meeting and Banquet in Trumann, Arkansas, where she will highlight the life and legacy of the late Retired Brig. Gen. Paul Rowlett, including his work on the high-profile Jessica Chambers case.

Apel’s remarks will focus on Rowlett’s distinguished career in military and intelligence service, as well as his involvement in complex criminal investigations. Rowlett, a Trumann High School graduate and United States Air Force Academy alumnus, rose to the rank of brigadier general in the Arkansas Air National Guard and served as an analyst with the U.S. Department of Justice.

From 2001 to 2023, Brig. Gen. Rowlett held key leadership roles in the Arkansas ANG, including Director of Operations and Commander of the 123rd Intelligence Squadron; Director of Intelligence (J2) for the Arkansas National Guard; and ultimately Chief of Staff of the Arkansas ANG. In these positions, he guided strategic planning, supported global ISR missions, strengthened cyber and space operations, and oversaw major personnel and readiness initiatives.

Rowlett deployed on several occasions to serve his country. He retired honorably in January 2023, concluding a distinguished career marked by exceptional leadership, courage, and devotion to the mission.

Among his notable contributions to justice in Mississippi, Rowlett assisted in the Chambers case, a widely followed Mississippi investigation that drew national attention. His expertise in intelligence and analysis was brought to bear on the case as investigators worked to piece together evidence in the 2014 killing.

Rowlett’s career spanned decades of service in both uniformed and civilian roles, much of it involving sensitive national security work. He died Nov. 29, 2025, in an automobile accident in Hattiesburg on his way to testify in the trial of Quinton Tellis, prompting an outpouring of recognition for his leadership and contributions. Tellis, who is still the main suspect in the Chambers case, is on trial for the stabbing death of Ming Chen “Mandy” Hsiao in Monroe, Louisiana.

Apel, founder and manager of Darkhorse Press in Jackson, Mississippi, is known for her extensive background in crime and investigative reporting across print, radio and television. Apel and Rowlett both worked on the Chambers case and other investigations over the years, as well as being personal friends.

The annual banquet is set for 6 p.m. Monday, March 30, at the Trumann Wildcat Center. The event is presented by Southern Bancorp.

The event was sold out but additional seating has been added, so for ticket information, contact the chamber office at 870-483-5424 or email [email protected] .

item.title: Cherokee Nation flutist Tommy Wildcat to perform at Natchez Powwow March 28-29 - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
NATCHEZ — Tommy Wildcat, a Cherokee Nation flute player, will perform at the Natchez Powwow on Saturday and Sunday, March 28 and 29, on the Natchez Bluff. Admission is free and open to the public.

Dr. Chuck Borum, who chairs the Natchez Powwow, said Wildcat is a great musician, and his performance will be an exciting and welcome addition to this year’s lineup.

item.title: Burned body found in wooded area off Greenway Drive, Jackson police say - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Jackson police are investigating after a burned body was discovered Tuesday in a wooded area off Greenway Drive, authorities said.

Officers and robbery-homicide detectives responded to the 2700 block of Greenway Drive on Tuesday after receiving a report of a burning body in the woods. When they arrived, they found what appeared to be the body of a man lying on the ground in what investigators described as a homeless encampment.

The body was burned beyond recognition, and the victim has not yet been identified, officials said.

The scene was processed by the Mobile Crime Unit, and the Hinds County coroner took custody of the body.

Detectives are continuing to follow up on leads in the case, which remains under investigation.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1234 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS.

item.title: Blue Springs man gets a decade for distributing child sexual abuse material - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
ABERDEEN — A Blue Springs man was sentenced Monday to 10 years in federal prison for distributing child sexual abuse material over a mobile application, according to court records.

Kristopher Brandon Holcomb, 44, was sentenced to 120 months in prison followed by 10 years of supervised release. He will also be required to register as a sex offender upon release.

According to court documents, Holcomb uploaded child sexual abuse material on a mobile application from July 2024 through May 2025. Investigators said he also communicated with individuals he believed to be minors and sent them illicit material.

Authorities reported that more than 60 videos and 192 images were found on Holcomb’s electronic devices during the investigation.

U.S. District Judge Sharion Aycock also ordered Holcomb to pay restitution to victims identified in the images and videos who requested compensation.

The case began with the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force through the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office and was later investigated by Homeland Security Investigations.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Parker S. King as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative aimed at combating child exploitation.

Officials said the effort brings together federal, state and local agencies to identify victims and prosecute offenders involved in online child exploitation.

item.title: Authorities seize meth, cocaine, MDMA in Tupelo drug bust - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A Tupelo man has been charged with multiple drug offenses after authorities executed a search warrant at a residence and seized large amounts of suspected narcotics, according to the Mississippi Department of Public Safety.

The Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics arrested 34-year-old Christopher Clay Beckwith on Wednesday, March 18, following an investigation into methamphetamine trafficking, the agency said. The Mississippi Highway Patrol and the DPS Interdiction Unit assisted in the investigation.

Beckwith was charged with aggravated trafficking of methamphetamine, trafficking of cocaine, possession with intent to sell or deliver hallucinogens, possession with intent to sell or deliver synthetic stimulants, and possession with intent to sell or deliver MDMA, commonly known as ecstasy.

Authorities said agents seized about 603.2 grams of methamphetamine, 30.7 grams of cocaine, 21 grams of MDMA and 2 grams of ketamine.

Investigators also reported seizing 31 dosage units of alprazolam, also known as Xanax, 13 dosage units of unknown white pills, three dosage units of unknown orange pills, about 40.4 grams of an unknown brown powder substance, two ledger books, two digital scales and $1,360 in cash believed to be proceeds from narcotics sales.

item.title: Wesson to host inaugural tablescape competition, silent auction for veterans programs - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
WESSON — The American Legion Auxiliary Unit 79 in Wesson will host its first tablescape competition and silent auction May 1-2 as part of the city’s Founder’s Day celebration, with proceeds supporting a range of veterans and community programs.

Organizers said funds raised from “The Heart of the Table” event will benefit initiatives including Girls State, the Auxiliary Emergency Fund, the Poppy Program, Wreaths Across America and the Veterans Affairs home in Collins.

The two-day event will feature a tablescape design competition at the Historic Old School and a silent auction held in conjunction with Founder’s Day activities at the park in Wesson.

Activities begin Friday, May 1, with contestants setting up their tablescapes from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. Judging is scheduled for Saturday morning, followed by a public exhibition from 1 to 5 p.m., during which attendees can vote for a People’s Choice winner. Admission and voting cost $1.

The silent auction will open at 8 a.m. Saturday at the park, close at 2 p.m., and reopen at 3 p.m. at the Historic Old School before concluding with a 5 p.m. closing ceremony announcing winners.

In addition to the competition and auction, the event will include family-friendly activities such as a photo booth, popcorn, educational displays about the American Legion Auxiliary’s mission, a children’s coloring station focused on Americanism and flag etiquette, and possible historical reenactments.

The tablescape competition is open to individuals, businesses and community groups, with entries judged on creativity, presentation, theme and craftsmanship. Participants will design themed table settings for round tables seating at least four people.

Organizers are also seeking sponsors, auction donations and monetary contributions. Donors will be recognized in event materials and provided documentation for tax purposes.

The event is being coordinated by a committee that includes Janet Currie, Dixie Thornton, Cathy Stroud and Judy Chester-Turner.

Organizers encourage community members to participate or attend, noting the event is designed to celebrate creativity while supporting veterans, military families and local programs.

item.title: Suspect arrested in connection with attempted armed robbery in Southaven - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
SOUTHAVEN — A man suspected in an attempted armed robbery earlier Sunday at a Goodman Road business has been arrested, according to Southaven Police.

Police said officers initially responded around 10:59 a.m. to a business in the 1000 block of Goodman Road East, where a white male suspect entered the store, went behind the counter and assaulted an employee while reportedly armed with a tool believed to be a screwdriver.

Investigators said the suspect attempted to access the cash register but did not appear to take anything. The employee fled the store, but the suspect chased her outside and pushed her to the ground before fleeing west toward Swinnea Road.

The victim sustained minor injuries and was treated at the scene by emergency medical personnel.

Authorities said the suspect was later identified as 54-year-old Larry Shawn Mayher, who is wanted for armed robbery in Southaven and is known to frequent Memphis, Tennessee.

Mayher was taken into custody around 8:45 p.m. Sunday during a traffic stop at Stateline Road and Assembly Street in Southaven. He is being held and will be transported to the DeSoto County Jail on an armed robbery charge.

Police credited tips from the public, along with investigative work by detectives and patrol officers, with helping lead to the arrest. The case remains under investigation.

item.title: Reeves declares Flood Insurance Awareness Week in Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Gov. Tate Reeves has declared March 22–28, 2026, as Flood Insurance Awareness Week at the request of the Mississippi Insurance Department, urging residents to consider coverage before disaster strikes.

State officials say more than one million properties in Mississippi lack flood insurance, despite repeated flooding events in recent years that have caused widespread financial losses.

“Mississippi has experienced significant flooding in recent years, causing hardship and financial loss for homeowners and business owners across our state,” Insurance Commissioner Mike Chaney said in a statement. “Many people underestimate the cost of flood damage, but even a few inches of water in a small home can lead to more than $10,000 in repairs.”

Officials emphasized that standard homeowners insurance policies do not cover flood damage. Flood insurance can be purchased through the National Flood Insurance Program or private insurers, but policies typically take 30 days to go into effect. As of the latest data, nearly 50,000 NFIP policies are active statewide.

Residents are encouraged to assess their flood risk using tools such as the Federal Emergency Management Agency Flood Map Service Center.

Preparedness efforts also include documenting personal property. The National Association of Insurance Commissioners offers a free Home Inventory App that allows users to catalog belongings and store records digitally for easy access after a disaster.

Officials recommend several steps to prepare for potential flooding, including signing up for local emergency alerts through systems like the Emergency Alert System and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Weather Radio, planning evacuation routes, safeguarding important documents, and assembling emergency supplies.

In the aftermath of a flood, residents should file insurance claims promptly, follow guidance from authorities, and avoid hazards such as contaminated water and electrical risks. Officials also warn that wildlife, including snakes, may enter homes during flooding and urge caution during cleanup.

More information about flood preparedness and recovery is available through FEMA and state emergency management resources.

item.title: Mississippi woman arrested in Colorado on parental kidnapping charge, child safely recovered - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
OLIVE BRANCH – A Mississippi woman wanted in connection with a parental kidnapping case out of Olive Branch was arrested in Colorado, and the child was safely recovered, according to Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office.

According to the Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office, Sharayon Brown, 28, was taken into custody after being located in Pueblo by members of the U.S. Marshals Violent Offender Task Force and local law enforcement agencies.

Authorities said the Olive Branch Police Department contacted the U.S. Marshals for the District of Colorado after receiving information that Brown, who was wanted in the abduction of her 11-year-old biological child from Olive Branch, could be in the Colorado Springs area.

Investigators searched several locations in Colorado Springs and located vehicles associated with Brown and the child. Agencies assisting in the search included the Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office, Fountain Police Department, Colorado Springs Police Department, El Paso County Sheriff’s Office and Colorado State Patrol.

Brown and the child were later found in the 3400 block of North Elizabeth Street in Pueblo, according to authorities. Brown was arrested on a Mississippi kidnapping warrant and booked into the Pueblo County Jail.

The child was safely recovered and transported by Pueblo sheriff’s detectives to the El Paso County Department of Human Services, where arrangements were being made for reunification with the custodial family.

Olive Branch Mayor Ken Adams thanked the Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office for its role in the arrest and recovery, along with the Olive Branch Police Department and the U.S. Marshals Violent Crime Task Force.
